CAVEMAN MODE ACTIVE — level: full

Respond terse like smart caveman. All technical substance stay. Only fluff die.

## Persistence

ACTIVE EVERY RESPONSE. No revert after many turns. No filler drift. Still active if unsure. Off only: "stop caveman" / "normal mode".

Default: **full**. Switch: `/caveman lite|full|ultra`.

## Rules

Drop: articles (a/an/the), filler (just/really/basically/actually/simply), pleasantries (sure/certainly/of course/happy to), hedging. Fragments OK. Short synonyms (big not extensive, fix not "implement a solution for"). Technical terms exact. Code blocks unchanged. Errors quoted exact.

Pattern: `[thing] [action] [reason]. [next step].`

Not: "Sure! I'd be happy to help you with that. The issue you're experiencing is likely caused by..."
Yes: "Bug in auth middleware. Token expiry check use `<` not `<=`. Fix:"

## Intensity

| Level | What change |
|-------|------------|
| **full** | Drop articles, fragments OK, short synonyms. Classic caveman |

Example — "Why React component re-render?"
- full: "New object ref each render. Inline object prop = new ref = re-render. Wrap in `useMemo`."

Example — "Explain database connection pooling."
- full: "Pool reuse open DB connections. No new connection per request. Skip handshake overhead."

## Auto-Clarity

Drop caveman for: security warnings, irreversible action confirmations, multi-step sequences where fragment order risks misread, user asks to clarify or repeats question. Resume caveman after clear part done.

Example — destructive op:
> **Warning:** This will permanently delete all rows in the `users` table and cannot be undone.
> ```sql
> DROP TABLE users;
> ```
> Caveman resume. Verify backup exist first.

## Boundaries

Code/commits/PRs: write normal. "stop caveman" or "normal mode": revert. Level persist until changed or session end.

## `search` has two filter paths, both narrow

**1. Known-key filters → server-side** (`search.go`)
`ParseSearchInput` scans the query for hardcoded prefixes — `author:`, `date:`, `branch:`, `repo:` — pulls them into typed `Config` fields (`Author`, `Date`, `Branch`, `Repos`), and the **server** does the filtering. `HasFilters()` just checks those fixed fields. Also exposed as cobra flags (`--author`, `--date`…). The keys are enumerated in code, one branch per key — not derived from data.

**2. Type-tab facet → client-side** (`search_tui.go:145` `filteredResults()`)
In the TUI only, filters already-loaded results by a single fixed dimension — `r.Type` equals checkpoint/commit/session. Equality on one hardcoded field. That's the entire client-side filter.

## What this means for your 9 lists

`search`'s model is **"enumerate the filterable keys per command, filter server-side."** Your control-plane lists **already do exactly that** — `repo mirror list` has `--cluster`, `--provider`, `--owner`, all server-side. So copying `search` = adding more typed server flags to each command individually. That is **not** a one-change-hits-all-9 win; it's per-command work, and it depends on the server supporting each filter.

The uniform win — filter all 9 lists with one edit — only exists at the `renderCoreList` layer, filtering the **rendered row cells client-side**. `search` does not do this (its client-side filter is just the coarse type facet).

So the real fork is:

| Approach | Coverage | Server dependency | Models after |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A. Client-side cell filter** in `renderCoreList` | all 9 lists, one edit | none — filters what's fetched | nothing existing (new, but tiny) |
| **B. `search`-style typed server flags** | per-command, incremental | needs server support per key | `search`, existing mirror flags |

"Filter all those commands at once" points at **A**. Want A, or per-command server-side flags like search, or a hybrid (A now, add typed server flags where the API supports it later)?

Yes — but narrowly, and already fully wired.

`ListMirrorsParams` (oas_parameters_gen.go:136) supports exactly three server-side filters:
- `Cluster` — exact, **case-sensitive**
- `Provider` — case-insensitive
- `Owner` — case-insensitive (upstream owner login)

Plus paging (`PageSize`, `PageToken`). No free-text search, no sort. All three are **already exposed** as `--cluster`/`--provider`/`--owner` (repo_mirror.go:410-412). So there's nothing left to add server-side for mirrors — the backend's filter surface is maxed out.

Two things worth noting for "improve filter across all 9":
1. **Server filters are per-endpoint and inconsistent.** Right below, `ListOIDCProvidersParams` and `ListOrgMembersParams` have **only** `PageSize`/`PageToken` — zero filters. So there is no uniform server-side filter to lean on across the 9 lists; each endpoint differs.
2. Mirror's server filters are **exact-match, single-value** (e.g. `--owner acme` = only that owner). No substring, no "contains", no multi-value.

So the gap a client-side cell filter fills, even for mirrors: substring/fuzzy matching, matching across columns at once (e.g. one term hitting name OR owner OR cluster), and — critically — a **consistent filter that works identically on all 9 lists** regardless of what each backend supports. Server-side can't give you that uniformity.

Want me to proceed planning the client-side cell filter at `renderCoreList` (approach A)?

# Upstream Core API fixes

This client carries workarounds for bugs/gaps in the control-plane
OpenAPI document and its surface. Each item below should be fixed at the
source (the control-plane service's spec generation / route design);
doing so lets us delete the corresponding workaround here and regenerate
a cleaner client. This file is the running checklist.

When an item is fixed upstream, remove its workaround (cited by file) and
delete the entry.

## 1. Operations enumerate every error status with no shared `default`

**Symptom:** each operation declares its real success code (good — 201
for creates, 200 for reads, 204 for deletes) but then lists every error
status separately (`400`, `401`, `403`, `422`, `500`, …) with no
`default` response. ogen turns that into a per-operation sum-type result,
forcing a type switch at every call site instead of the ergonomic
`(*T, error)`.

**Fix upstream:** emit a single `default` error response (every error
already references the same `ErrorModel`, so a `default` is lossless).
ogen then generates "convenient errors" — `(*T, error)` with non-2xx as a
typed `*ErrorModelStatusCode` — straight from the spec.

**Workaround:** `spec/normalize.go` (`foldErrorResponses`) folds each
operation's explicit 4xx/5xx into one `default`, keeping the real success
code untouched. This is the one transform that is a deliberate
ergonomics choice rather than a pure bug workaround; a shared `default`
upstream retires it.

<!-- Resolved upstream and removed:
  - Nullable arrays (`"type": ["array","null"]`) — entiredb now emits
    non-nullable arrays (`"type": "array"`, absent ⇒ `[]`), so the
    `collapseTypeUnions` transform is gone.
  - by-mirror lookup vs mirrorId delete — entiredb ENT-741 replaced the
    two-call lookup→delete with a single delete-by-coords route
    (`DELETE /mirrors?provider&owner&repo&clusterHost`); `mirror remove`
    now calls it directly and surfaces the new 404/403/503 contract. -->

# Plan: client-side `--filter` for `entire repo mirror list`

## Context

`entire repo mirror list` prints every mirror the logged-in user can see. As
mirror counts grow, the flat list becomes hard to scan — the two things a user
needs are **find** (locate a specific mirror) and **explore** (narrow the set).

The backend (`GET /mirrors`) already offers exact-match server filters
`--cluster` / `--provider` / `--owner`, but has **no filter on the repo name**
and no substring/free-text match. True server-side filtering can't be improved
from this repo: the CLI is a client-only ogen consumer (`ogen.yml` disables the
server half) and the query/match logic lives in the separate **entiredb**
backend (see `internal/coreapi/UPSTREAM.md`, `gen.go`). Scope is deliberately
**this repo only**, so the in-repo win is a **client-side filter** that narrows
the already-fetched rows by substring — matching exactly what the user sees in
the table (`owner/repo`, clone URL, private flag).

Outcome: `entire repo mirror list --filter payments` shows only rows whose
displayed cells contain `payments` (case-insensitive), applied identically to
the table and `--json` output, and composing with the existing server filters.

## Approach

Add one flag, filter client-side on the rendered row cells, via a small generic
helper. No changes to the shared `renderCoreList` scaffold — the filter is
applied inside the existing fetch closures in `repo_mirror.go`, so blast radius
is limited to this command.

### 1. Generic helper — `cmd/entire/cli/corecmd.go`

Add next to `printTable` (reuses the same `row func(T) []string` every list
already defines, so it is trivially reusable if another list wants it later —
only wired to mirror list now):

```go
// filterByRow keeps items whose rendered row cells contain term
// (case-insensitive substring, matched across all columns). An empty term
// returns items unchanged. Matching the display cells means the filter acts on
// exactly what the user sees in the table.
func filterByRow[T any](items []T, row func(T) []string, term string) []T {
    if term == "" {
        return items
    }
    term = strings.ToLower(term)
    out := items[:0:0] // new backing array; preserve nil-vs-empty for JSON
    for _, it := range items {
        for _, cell := range row(it) {
            if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(cell), term) {
                out = append(out, it)
                break
            }
        }
    }
    return out
}
```

### 2. Wire the flag — `cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror.go` (`newRepoMirrorListCmd`)

- Declare `var filter string` alongside `cluster, provider, owner`.
- Register: `cmd.Flags().StringVar(&filter, "filter", "", "Filter results by substring match on any displayed column (case-insensitive)")`.
- In **both** `runCoreList` closures (existing mirrors at :373 and
  `--show-available` at :354), after the items are fetched and before returning,
  narrow them:
  - mirrors: `mirrors = filterByRow(mirrors, mirrorRow, filter)`
  - available: `avail = filterByRow(avail, availableMirrorRow, filter)`
  Filtering inside the closure means it runs before both the JSON and table
  branches of `renderCoreList`, so `--json --filter x` returns the filtered set.

The existing empty-state sentences ("No mirrors found." / "No repos available to
mirror.") already cover a filtered-to-empty result acceptably; no new message
needed.

## Files

- `cmd/entire/cli/corecmd.go` — add `filterByRow[T]` helper (`strings` already imported).
- `cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror.go` — add `--filter` flag + apply in both list closures.
- `cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror_test.go` — tests (existing `serveMirrorList` fake control-plane harness).

## Tests (TDD — write first)

In `repo_mirror_test.go`, using the existing fake-control-plane harness:

1. `--filter` narrows table output to matching rows only (match on repo name, and on owner).
2. Case-insensitivity: `--filter PAY` matches `owner/payments`.
3. `--filter` + `--json`: JSON output contains only matching items (and stays `[]`, not `null`, when nothing matches).
4. Empty `--filter ""` (default) returns the full list unchanged.
5. `--filter` applies under `--show-available` too.
6. Unit test `filterByRow` directly: any-column match, empty term passthrough, no-match returns empty (non-nil) slice.

## Verification

```bash
mise run fmt && mise run lint
mise run test        # unit + the new mirror-list filter tests
```

End-to-end against the fake control plane is covered by the table/JSON tests
above. Manual smoke (optional, needs a real login):

```bash
entire repo mirror list --filter <substr>
entire repo mirror list --filter <substr> --json
entire repo mirror list --show-available --filter <substr>
```

  displayed cell contains `payments`.

  **REPO** column contains `cli`.

```go
    col  string
    term string
}

// parseRowFilter splits "col=term" into a scoped clause; a bare "term" (no '=')
// is an any-column clause. Values are lowercased for case-insensitive matching.
func parseRowFilter(raw string) rowFilter {
    if k, v, ok := strings.Cut(raw, "="); ok {
        return rowFilter{col: strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(k)), term: strings.ToLower(v)}
    }
    return rowFilter{term: strings.ToLower(raw)}

// typo fails loudly instead of silently returning nothing. No clauses => items
```

# Plan: client-side `--filter` for `entire repo mirror list`

## Context

`entire repo mirror list` prints every mirror the logged-in user can see. As
mirror counts grow, the flat list becomes hard to scan — the two things a user
needs are **find** (locate a specific mirror) and **explore** (narrow the set).

The backend (`GET /mirrors`) already offers exact-match server filters
`--cluster` / `--provider` / `--owner`, but has **no filter on the repo name**
and no substring/free-text match. True server-side filtering can't be improved
from this repo: the CLI is a client-only ogen consumer (`ogen.yml` disables the
server half) and the query/match logic lives in the separate **entiredb**
backend (see `internal/coreapi/UPSTREAM.md`, `gen.go`). Scope is deliberately
**this repo only**, so the in-repo win is a **client-side filter** that narrows
the already-fetched rows by substring — matching exactly what the user sees in
the table (`owner/repo`, clone URL, private flag).

Outcome: two filter forms, both case-insensitive substring, both applied
identically to table and `--json` and composing with the existing server
filters:

- `entire repo mirror list --filter payments` — bare term: keep rows where **any**
  displayed cell contains `payments`.
- `entire repo mirror list --filter repo=cli` — column-scoped: keep rows where the
  **REPO** column contains `cli`.
- Repeatable and ANDed: `--filter repo=cli --filter private=yes`.

Plus a sort option, ordering on the same rendered cells:

- **Default (no flag): sorted by repo name ascending** — the list is always
  deterministically ordered (today it's arbitrary server order).
- `--sort private` — sort by the named column (header, case-insensitive).
- `--sort -repo` — leading `-` = descending.
- Unknown column errors the same way `--filter` does.

## Approach

Add one repeatable flag, filter client-side on the rendered row cells via a
small generic helper. No changes to the shared `renderCoreList` scaffold — the
filter is applied inside the existing fetch closures in `repo_mirror.go`, so
blast radius is limited to this command.

### 1. Generic helper — `cmd/entire/cli/corecmd.go`

Add next to `printTable` (reuses the `headers` + `row func(T) []string` every
list already defines, so it is trivially reusable later — only wired to mirror
list now):

```go
// rowFilter is one parsed --filter clause: term is a case-insensitive substring;
// col (a lowercased header name, "" = any column) scopes it to one column.
type rowFilter struct {
    col  string
    term string
}

// parseRowFilter splits "col=term" into a scoped clause; a bare "term" (no '=')
// is an any-column clause. Values are lowercased for case-insensitive matching.
func parseRowFilter(raw string) rowFilter {
    if k, v, ok := strings.Cut(raw, "="); ok {
        return rowFilter{col: strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(k)), term: strings.ToLower(v)}
    }
    return rowFilter{term: strings.ToLower(raw)}
}

// filterRows keeps items whose rendered cells satisfy EVERY clause (AND). A bare
// clause matches if any cell contains its term; a scoped clause matches only its
// named column. An unknown column name is an error (listing valid columns), so a
// typo fails loudly instead of silently returning nothing. No clauses => items
// unchanged. Matching display cells means the filter acts on exactly what the
// user sees in the table.
func filterRows[T any](items []T, headers []string, row func(T) []string, clauses []string) ([]T, error) {
    filters := make([]rowFilter, 0, len(clauses))
    for _, c := range clauses {
        if c == "" {
            continue
        }
        f := parseRowFilter(c)
        if f.col != "" && headerIndex(headers, f.col) < 0 {
            return nil, fmt.Errorf("unknown filter column %q; valid columns: %s", f.col, strings.ToLower(strings.Join(headers, ", ")))
        }
        filters = append(filters, f)
    }
    if len(filters) == 0 {
        return items, nil
    }
    out := items[:0:0] // new backing array; preserve nil-vs-empty for JSON
    for _, it := range items {
        cells := row(it)
        if matchesAll(cells, headers, filters) {
            out = append(out, it)
        }
    }
    return out, nil
}
```

Plus tiny helpers `headerIndex(headers []string, name string) int` (case-insensitive
lookup, -1 if absent) and `matchesAll(cells, headers []string, filters []rowFilter) bool`
(bare clause → any-cell `strings.Contains`; scoped clause → `Contains` on the
resolved column index).

### 2. Sort helper — `cmd/entire/cli/corecmd.go`

```go
// sortRows orders items by the rendered value of one column, in place. spec is a
// header name; a leading '-' sorts descending. An empty spec sorts by the first
// column (the primary identifier) ascending — so lists are always deterministic.
// Unknown column => error naming valid columns. Comparison is case-insensitive
// string order on the display cell (same values the filter matches). The sort
// key for each item is computed once (not per comparison).
func sortRows[T any](items []T, headers []string, row func(T) []string, spec string) error {
    desc := strings.HasPrefix(spec, "-")
    name := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(strings.TrimPrefix(spec, "-")))
    idx := 0
    if name != "" {
        if idx = headerIndex(headers, name); idx < 0 {
            return fmt.Errorf("unknown sort column %q; valid columns: %s", name, strings.ToLower(strings.Join(headers, ", ")))
        }
    }
    keys := make([]string, len(items))
    for i, it := range items {
        keys[i] = strings.ToLower(cellAt(row(it), idx))
    }
    sort.SliceStable(items, func(a, b int) bool {
        if desc {
            return keys[a] > keys[b]
        }
        return keys[a] < keys[b]
    })
    return nil
}
```

Note: `sort.SliceStable` swaps `items` but not `keys`, so precompute an index
permutation instead — sort an `[]int` of indices by `keys`, then rebuild `items`
in that order. (Small refinement over the sketch above; keeps keys aligned.)
`cellAt(cells []string, i int) string` returns `cells[i]` or `""` if out of range.

### 3. Wire the flags — `cmd/entire/cli/repo_mirror.go` (`newRepoMirrorListCmd`)

- Declare `var filters []string` and `var sortSpec string` alongside `cluster, provider, owner`.
- Register:
  - `cmd.Flags().StringArrayVar(&filters, "filter", nil, "Filter rows by case-insensitive substring; bare term matches any column, or COLUMN=term scopes to one column (e.g. repo=cli). Repeatable (ANDed).")`

  Doing this inside the closure means filter+sort run before both the JSON and
  table branches of `renderCoreList`, so `--json` reflects the same ordered,

mirror.") already cover a filtered-to-empty result acceptably; no new message

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Manual test for `entire repo mirror list --filter/--sort`.
# Runs against your REAL active login (no fake backend possible for a built
# binary), so you need to be logged in and have at least a couple of mirrors.
#
# Usage:
#   ./test-mirror-filter-sort.sh
#
# It builds a throwaway binary, then walks each behavior printing the command
# and what to look for. Read the "EXPECT" line under each step.

set -euo pipefail

REPO_ROOT="/Users/gtrrz-victor/wks/cli/cli"
BIN="$(mktemp -d)/entire"

cd "$REPO_ROOT"

echo "==> Building entire binary..."
go build -o "$BIN" ./cmd/entire
echo "    built: $BIN"
echo

# Fail early with a friendly message if not logged in.
if ! "$BIN" auth status >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  echo "!! Not logged in. Run '! entire login' first, then re-run this script." >&2
  exit 1
fi

run() {
  echo "-------------------------------------------------------------------------"
  echo "\$ entire $*"
  echo
  "$BIN" "$@" || echo "(command exited non-zero — expected for the error cases below)"
  echo
}

echo "#########################################################################"
echo "# 1. Baseline — default sort is by repo name (ascending)"
echo "#    EXPECT: rows ordered A→Z by the REPO column"
echo "#########################################################################"
run repo mirror list

echo "#########################################################################"
echo "# 2. Bare --filter (matches ANY column, case-insensitive substring)"
echo "#    Replace 'a' below with a substring you know appears in a repo/owner."
echo "#    EXPECT: only rows containing that substring anywhere"
echo "#########################################################################"
run repo mirror list --filter a

echo "#########################################################################"
echo "# 3. Column-scoped --filter repo=<substr>"
echo "#    EXPECT: only rows whose REPO column contains the substring."
echo "#    A value that appears only in another column must NOT match here."
echo "#########################################################################"
run repo mirror list --filter repo=e

echo "#########################################################################"
echo "# 4. Repeatable --filter (ANDed — every clause must match)"
echo "#    EXPECT: strictly fewer/equal rows than either clause alone"
echo "#########################################################################"
run repo mirror list --filter repo=e --filter private=no

echo "#########################################################################"
echo "# 5. --sort by a named column (header name, case-insensitive)"
echo "#    EXPECT: rows ordered by the PRIVATE column (no before yes)"
echo "#########################################################################"
run repo mirror list --sort private

echo "#########################################################################"
echo "# 6. Descending sort with leading '-'"
echo "#    EXPECT: same rows as step 1 but in reverse repo-name order"
echo "#########################################################################"
run repo mirror list --sort -repo

echo "#########################################################################"
echo "# 7. --filter + --json (filter applies to JSON too; empty set is [] not null)"
echo "#    EXPECT: JSON array containing only matching mirrors"
echo "#########################################################################"

content.text:
Everything needed is available: `atotto/clipboard` is already a dep, and we're on bubbletea v2 (has mouse support). The clone URL in the table (`entire://<cluster>/gh/<owner>/<repo>`) is exactly what `entire repo clone` accepts, so clicking a row would copy `entire repo clone entire://…`.

Design constraints I'll honor:
- **Keep the plain table as the non-interactive fallback** (CLAUDE.md requires it — agents/pipes/`--json`/`ACCESSIBLE` must still work). So the TUI is an interactive-only layer on top.
- **Mouse + keyboard both**: click a row to copy, and ↑/↓ + Enter to copy (no-mouse terminals, accessibility), `q`/Esc to quit. Note: enabling mouse capture disables the terminal's native drag-to-select while the TUI is open — a reason to make it opt-in.
- Clipboard can fail on headless/SSH (no `pbcopy`/`xclip`); I'll show the result inline rather than crash.

One real fork before I build:

# Ship Changes

Commit current changes, push to remote, and update the PR.

## Step 1: Analyze changes

1. Run `git diff --stat` and `git diff` to understand what changed
2. Run `git status` to see untracked files
3. Run `git log --oneline -3` to match the repo's commit message style

## Step 2: Commit

1. Stage only the relevant changed/untracked files by name (never `git add -A` or `git add .`)
2. Write a concise commit message that focuses on the "why" not the "what"
   - If `` is provided, use it as the commit message
   - Otherwise, draft one from the diff
3. Commit. If hooks fail, diagnose and fix — do NOT use `--no-verify`

## Step 3: Push

1. Check if the branch tracks a remote: `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref --symbolic-full-name @{u}`
2. If not tracking, push with `-u origin <branch>`
3. If tracking, just `git push`
4. If push is rejected (remote has new commits), pull with rebase first then push

## Step 4: Update PR

1. Find the open PR for the current branch: `gh pr view --json number,body,title`
2. If no PR exists, skip this step and inform the user
3. Compare the current PR body against the new changes:
   - If the changes are within the existing PR scope, update the description to reflect the current state
   - If the changes are additive or a follow-up, add a PR comment summarizing what was just pushed instead
4. When updating the PR body, preserve the overall structure but refresh the summary bullets and test plan
5. When adding a comment, keep it concise — bullet points of what changed and why
6. **Before making any PR update (description edit or comment), show the user the exact text you plan to post and ask for their approval. Do NOT post until they confirm.**

## Rules

- Never commit files that look like secrets (.env, credentials, tokens)
- Never force push
- Always show the user what was committed and the PR URL when done

**Title:** `repo mirror list: add --repo filter and --sort`

**Body:**
```markdown
## What

Makes `entire repo mirror list` easier to scan as mirror counts grow.

- **`--repo <substr>`** — client-side, case-insensitive substring filter on the
  repo name. The control plane already filters by `--owner`/`--provider`/`--cluster`
  server-side but not by repo name, so this fills that gap. Applies to the table,
  `--json`, and `--show-available`.
- **`--sort <column>`** — sort by a displayed column (header name, case-insensitive);
  a leading `-` sorts descending (e.g. `--sort -repo`).
- **Deterministic default order** — owner/repo ascending, breaking duplicate-repo
  ties (same repo mirrored on several clusters) by cluster host, instead of
  arbitrary server order.

Columns are unchanged (`REPO`, `CLONE URL`, `PRIVATE`).

## Why

The list printed in arbitrary order with no way to narrow it. Server-side repo
filtering would require an entiredb change; `--repo` is the in-repo win. Shared
`sortRows`/`filterByRepo` helpers keep it reusable across control-plane lists.

## Test plan

- Unit + command-level tests: `--repo` filtering, `--sort` (asc/desc, unknown
  column errors), default owner/repo ordering with cluster tiebreak, `--json`
  and `--show-available` paths.
- `mise run fmt` clean; golangci-lint (v2) 0 issues; full `cmd/entire/cli` package passes.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
```
